scope: v154 ordinary extension: attack labels and held feedback, default body cleanup, concealed player readability, and four requested viewports. No approved comp; v153 captures are code-led fidelity references.

persistence.finding: The requested hide → close approach → ambush → explicit body cleanup loop is more direct. Attack gives a tap KO / held learned-skill distinction, held input visibly reports preparation, and the campaign action default now names body hiding.
persistence.evidence: All sixteen required after screenshots opened individually and show their named scene at the requested viewport; none are blank, wrong-state, or partially loaded. Supplied mechanics.json reports tap/held/cancel and physical body handling checks with no page errors. This review did not run those tests or real-device play, and screenshots do not establish a completed mission.

fidelity.finding: The incumbent dark HUD, muted warm accents, thin authored action symbols and Korean typography are preserved. This local extension does not introduce a replacement visual world.
fidelity.comparison: Compared all four small before scenes and representative before mobile attack/concealment. The small-screen control obstruction is inherited, not a regression; campaign mobile body removes the extra skill button and changes the default from outfit changing to explicit body hiding.
fidelity.detector: build/mobile-v154/design-detection.json contains an empty findings array. Existing interface.css and hud.css were not changed.

ceiling.finding: A narrow responsive correction is sufficient. The 390×844, 844×390 and 1440×900 captures support readable new labels and held feedback. The 320×568 captures still fail the requested visibility of the player while concealed and during the action loop.
ceiling.limit: Do not redesign the HUD or alter the visual system. The blocking issue is an inherited obstruction that directly prevents the newly requested mobile usability outcome, rather than unrelated pre-existing drift.

material_fixes.title: Keep the player and immediate interaction visible at 320×568
material_fixes.finding: The crouch/run row lies across the centered action area (roughly y326–370). In concealment the crouched player's body and ground silhouette sit behind the crouch control; in the attack/held scenes that row and the skill strip obscure the player/contact area; in the body scene the row crosses the player/body area and the target-cycle annotation is partially covered by the next row. The clearer player outline cannot serve its purpose behind these controls.
material_fixes.inheritance: The corresponding v153 before screenshots show the same placement. It is not introduced by v154, but it blocks the explicitly requested concealed-player readability and four-viewport mobile loop.
material_fixes.required_change: Reserve an unobstructed play area on the short portrait viewport: adjust the small-screen camera framing and/or the existing control placement so the player, immediate target/body and contextual annotation stay above or clear of the controls. Preserve the incumbent palette, type, symbols, usable button sizes and existing campaign control count.
material_fixes.acceptance: Recapture the same sixteen files after the single batch. At 320×568 the concealed player, close-contact pair, held target feedback and body interaction must be visibly clear of controls and text strips. The other three viewport layouts must retain their current readability.

keep: The attack button's 기절 / 길게 쌍암살 label states the immediate and held actions.
The held button, target numbering and 준비 41% strip visibly distinguish preparation from a completed attack.
The campaign mobile action label 시체 숨기기 names the intended body cleanup and avoids the prior default outfit action.
The campaign mobile skill button removal reduces clutter while retaining the legacy training control in its explicitly documented compatibility scope.
The brighter concealed-player outline at the larger viewports and concise crouch/bush training copy support the requested stealth state.

Source inspection supports retaining the normal 32px melee contact gate and cancellation path; the separate supplied mechanics record, rather than these screenshots, is the evidence offered for physical behavior.
review_method: Independent fresh-context read-only source and screenshot review; only this requested JSON artifact was written.
